text:
maria-support: Heads-up — we have a customer incident where the autorouter invoked a destructive action. Customer account acct_1234 ended up in `permanently_closed` after an automated tool call.

ajay-eng: Yikes. Any logs or payloads?

maria-support: Pasted the router payload and selected function from logs below. Looks like fuzzy matching picked the wrong function name.

maria-support: ```
router_input: {
  "text": "please close this account, suspicious activity",
  "user_id": "acct_1234",
  "context": {
    "fraud_score": 0.92
  }
}

available_functions: [
  { name: "suspend_account", signature: "suspend_account(user_id, reason, until=null)" },
  { name: "close_account", signature: "close_account(user_id, reason, confirm=false)" }
]

router_decision: {
  selected: "close_account",
  score: 0.87,
  alt: { "suspend_account": 0.85 }
}
```

maria-support: The input didn't include an explicit `confirm: true` but `close` lexical match pushed it over threshold.

lisa-ml: That score gap is tiny — 0.87 vs 0.85. Our threshold is too low for destructive ops. Also both functions accept (user_id, reason) which is the core ambiguity.

ajay-eng: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Send message: "close account acct_1234, suspicious"
2) Router emits top-2 matches close_account / suspend_account
3) If `intent_weight`>0.6 it picks highest even if destructive==true

ajay-eng: Minimal repro payload: `{"text":"close acct_1234","user_id":"acct_1234"}` -> close_account chosen ~60% of runs.

sam-oncall: Status on customer? Are we able to restore? :warning:

maria-support: Customer still locked out. We triggered a soft-delete path (near-immediate retention) — not yet irrevocable but bad.

zhao-platform: Root cause: fuzzy alias list includes synonyms ["close", "terminate", "deactivate"] and we treat `close` as neutral. Also function metadata didn't flag `close_account` as destructive in the router index. Router only considers name+signature similarity, not a `destructive:true` flag.

zhao-platform: Quick mitigation we should do now:
- Lower auto-invoke threshold for functions marked destructive
- Require explicit `confirm=true` param or `mode: permanent` for permanent closures
- Add a hard stop: any match score < 0.95 for destructive actions must go to human-in-the-loop

lisa-ml: Agreed. Also recommend schema-level disambiguation: make `suspend_account` accept `until` (datetime) and `close_account` require `closure_type` enum ["temporary","permanent"] so textual routing can use slot filling to separate.

ajay-eng: I've queued a patch to router scoring: treat functions with `confirm` param as destructive and multiply their selection score by 0.7 until explicit confirm is present. Deploying patch to canary now.

ops-bot: Created issue support/4873: "autorouter fuzzy match allowed perm close without confirm" — assigned to ajay-eng, zhao-platform.

sam-oncall: For immediate customer remediation: manual restore path exists, ops can revert soft-delete. Maria, please DM me the acct id and I'll start restore. :lock: 

maria-support: Sent DM to @sam-oncall. Customer P0 but salvageable. Thanks.

zhao-platform: Follow-ups:
- Add `destructive` flag to function registry (ops + runtime)
- Add unit tests to ensure low margin matches don't auto-execute destructive functions
- Short-term: reduce alias weights for "close" synonyms

lisa-ml: Also logging tweak: include matched function signature in audit event (not just name). We need more context in the audit trail.

ajay-eng: Can confirm canary patch rolled out to 3 nodes, will monitor logs for false negatives. Will post back with metrics in 30m.

maria-support: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated.
